title: School completion, SDG regions compared, by sex
headline: Primary completion for all by 2030 needs the rate in Sub-Saharan Africa to rise 5.4 points a year
subtitle: Percentage of a cohort of children or young people aged 3-5 years above the intended age for the last grade of primary education who have completed primary education
years: In Sub-Saharan Africa it has risen 0.9 points a year, from 46.3% in 2000 to 67.5% in 2024.
data_line: Data: UNESCO UIS via UN SDG Global Database, series SE_TOT_CPLR, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Primary completion for all by 2030 needs the rate in Sub-Saharan Africa to rise 5.4 points a year. In Sub-Saharan Africa it has risen 0.9 points a year, from 46.3% in 2000 to 67.5% in 2024. Sub-Saharan Africa: 0.9 a year observed, 5.4 needed; Oceania (excl. Aus., NZ): 0.4 a year observed, 5.1 needed; World: 0.4 a year observed, 2.0 needed; Central and S. Asia: 0.9 a year observed, 1.9 needed; N. Africa and W. Asia: 0.7 a year observed, 1.7 needed; Latin America, Caribbean: 0.5 a year observed, 1.1 needed; E. and S.-E. Asia: 0.3 a year observed, 0.3 needed; Australia and NZ: 0.0 a year observed, 0.1 needed; Europe and N. America: 0.0 a year observed, 0.0 needed
method: Method: linear pace on published aggregates, from 2000 for Sub-Saharan Africa.
question: Which countries in Sub-Saharan Africa have moved primary completion fastest, and how?
